literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 本文提供了关于汉坦病毒生物学、流行病学、临床表现、诊断策略和新兴治疗方案的更新且综合的概述。它突出了分子病毒学、基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术、单克隆抗体疗法以及下一代疫苗平台在解决当前知识空白中的重要性。 [10.5501/wjv.120334]
近期公共卫生警报重新引起了对汉坦病毒感染的关注,这是一种罕见但可能严重的人兽共患病。1,2 对风湿病学家而言,其相关性具有选择性,但在符合的情况下具有重要的临床意义。 [10.3899/jrheum.2026-0485]
本研究报告了汉坦病毒株在本土鼩鼱、啮齿动物和蝙蝠中的存在,包括致命的Sangassou病毒,表明这些病毒在非洲广泛传播但未被检测到。 [10.1038/s44360-026-00200-3]
我们推导了栖息地平衡、基本再生数R0以及时间依赖的有效再生数Re(t),并评估了在退化-恢复情景下的感染负担和阈值指标。 [10.3390/v18091024]
心包积液和其他一些发现与严重疾病有关。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014609]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The article provides an updated and integrated overview of hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic strategies, and emerging therapeutic approaches. [10.5501/wjv.120334]

Recent public health alerts have renewed attention to hantavirus infection, an uncommon but potentially severe zoonosis.1,2 For rheumatologists, its relevance is selective but clinically important in compatible contexts. [10.3899/jrheum.2026-0485]

The study reports the presence of hantavirus strains, including the lethal Sangassou virus, in native shrews, rodents, and bats, indicating a widespread but undetected circulation of these viruses. [10.1038/s44360-026-00200-3]

We derived the habitat equilibrium, the basic reproduction number R0, and the time-dependent effective reproduction number Re(t) and evaluated infection-burden and threshold indicators across degradation-restoration scenarios. [10.3390/v18091024]
Pericardial effusions and several other findings were associated with severe disease. [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014609]

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. The article provides an updated and integrated overview of hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic strategies, and emerging therapeutic approaches. [10.5501/wjv.120334]. Recent public health alerts have renewed attention to hantavirus infection, an uncommon but potentially severe zoonosis.1,2 For rheumatologists, its relevance is selective but clinically important in compatible contexts. The study reports the presence of hantavirus strains, including the lethal Sangassou virus, in native shrews, rodents, and bats, indicating a widespread but undetected circulation of these viruses. We derived the habitat equilibrium, the basic reproduction number R0, and the time-dependent effective reproduction number Re(t) and evaluated infection-burden and threshold indicators across degradation-restoration scenarios.

news.headline_zh: 西班牙接受载有汉坦病毒暴发的邮轮。
news.lead_zh: 西班牙同意接受一艘因汉坦病毒暴发而被隔离的邮轮,世卫组织协调欧盟提出请求。
key_findings_zh: 西班牙同意接受一艘载有汉坦病毒暴发的邮轮。
邮轮上有7名乘客被确认感染,3人死亡,1人危重。
欧洲疾病预防控制中心将在邮轮抵达西班牙港口前进行评估。
所有乘客将在抵达后接受医疗检查并被遣返。
西班牙批准荷兰请求,允许医生通过特别航班前往加那利群岛。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 汉坦病毒在邮轮上的暴发引发国际关注,但对一般人群的风险仍被认为较低。
news.caveats_zh: 事件细节仍需进一步确认,且部分信息基于世卫组织的初步评估。
news.headline_en: Spain Accepts Cruise Ship with Hantavirus Outbreak Onboard.
news.lead_en: Spain has agreed to accept a cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak onboard, as requested by the World Health Organization in coordination with the European Union.
key_findings_en: Spain has agreed to accept a cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak onboard.
Seven passengers have been confirmed infected, with three deaths and one in critical condition.
The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) will conduct a situation assessment before the ship arrives in a Spanish port.
All passengers will undergo medical examination, receive necessary care, and be repatriated upon arrival.
Spain has granted a separate request from the Netherlands for a doctor to be transported to the Canary Islands on a special medical flight.
news.trend_or_risk_en: The hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship has raised international concerns, but the risk to the general population is considered low.
news.caveats_en: Event details are still under investigation, and some information is based on preliminary assessments by the WHO.
news.brief_en: Spain has agreed to accept a cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak onboard, as requested by the World Health Organization in coordination with the European Union. The ship is currently moored off the coast of Cape Verde, with 147 people on board. According to the WHO, seven passengers have been confirmed infected, with three deaths and one patient in critical condition. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) will conduct a situation assessment before the ship arrives in a Spanish port. Upon arrival, all passengers will undergo a medical examination, receive necessary care, and be repatriated. Additionally, Spain granted a separate request from the Netherlands for a doctor to be transported to the Canary Islands on a special medical flight.

papers.title: Habitat-Mediated Spillover Risk of Andes Hantavirus in Oligoryzomys longicaudatus: A Mechanistic Eco-Epidemiological Model
papers.abstract: Andes hantavirus (ANDV) is a rodent-borne orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in southern South America. Its maintenance and spillover risk depend on the ecology of its principal reservoir, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus, and on environmental changes that alter habitat availability, host abundance, and human–rodent interfaces. We developed a mechanistic eco-epidemiological model that couples effective habitat cover to an SIR framework for ANDV transmission in O. Habitat degradation and compensatory restoration modify rodent carrying capacity, natality, and the force of infection, which depends on infected host load relative to instantaneous ecological capacity. We derived the habitat equilibrium, the basic reproduction number R0, and the time-dependent effective reproduction number Re(t) and evaluated infection-burden and threshold indicators across degradation-restoration scenarios. The analysis shows that R0 is independent of equilibrium habitat cover because susceptible abundance scales with carrying capacity at the disease-free equilibrium. In contrast, Re(t), cumulative incidence, and infected load depend on transient habitat-mediated crowding. Restoration increases reservoir abundance and absolute infection burden, whereas degradation can reduce abundance while increasing crowding-driven transmission pressure and prolonging supercritical windows. These results identify ecological conditions under which habitat change may intensify reservoir infection pressure and guide One Health surveillance at human–rodent interfaces.

papers.title_zh: 栖息地介导的安第斯病毒在长尾小鼠中的风险:一个机制性生态流行病学模型
papers.source_body_en: Andes hantavirus (ANDV) is a rodent-borne orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in southern South America. Its maintenance and spillover risk depend on the ecology of its principal reservoir, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus, and on environmental changes that alter habitat availability, host abundance, and human–rodent interfaces. We developed a mechanistic eco-epidemiological model that couples effective habitat cover to an SIR framework for ANDV transmission in O. Habitat degradation and compensatory restoration modify rodent carrying capacity, natality, and the force of infection, which depends on infected host load relative to instantaneous ecological capacity. We derived the habitat equilibrium, the basic reproduction number R0, and the time-dependent effective reproduction number Re(t) and evaluated infection-burden and threshold indicators across degradation-restoration scenarios. The analysis shows that R0 is independent of equilibrium habitat cover because susceptible abundance scales with carrying capacity at the disease-free equilibrium. In contrast, Re(t), cumulative incidence, and infected load depend on transient habitat-mediated crowding. Restoration increases reservoir abundance and absolute infection burden, whereas degradation can reduce abundance while increasing crowding-driven transmission pressure and prolonging supercritical windows. These results identify ecological conditions under which habitat change may intensify reservoir infection pressure and guide One Health surveillance at human–rodent interfaces.
papers.abstract_zh: 安第斯病毒(ANDV)是一种由啮齿动物传播的正汉坦病毒,与南美洲南部的汉坦病毒肺综合征相关。其维持和风险取决于其主要储存宿主长尾小鼠(Oligoryzomys longicaudatus)的生态以及环境变化,这些变化会改变栖息地可用性、啮齿动物数量和人类-啮齿动物接触界面。我们开发了一个机制性生态流行病学模型,将有效栖息地覆盖与ANDV在O. longicaudatus中的SIR框架耦合。栖息地退化和补偿性恢复会改变啮齿动物的承载能力、出生率以及感染力,而感染力取决于感染啮齿动物的载量与瞬时生态容量的相对关系。我们推导了栖息地平衡、基本再生数R0以及时间依赖的有效再生数Re(t),并评估了在退化-恢复情景下的感染负担和阈值指标。分析表明,R0与平衡栖息地覆盖无关,因为易感个体数量在无病状态下与承载能力成比例。相反,Re(t)、累积感染数和感染载量取决于瞬时栖息地介导的拥挤情况。恢复会增加啮齿动物数量和绝对感染负担,而退化可能减少数量,同时增加由拥挤驱动的感染压力并延长超临界窗口。这些结果确定了栖息地变化可能加剧感染压力的生态条件,并指导人类-啮齿动物接触界面的One Health策略。

papers.title: Hantavirus: biology, immune responses, and pathogenesis
papers.abstract: Abstract The recent Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise has raised global public health alarms due to its dangerous ability to person-to-person spread. Hantavirus infections primarily manifest as hemorrhagic fever with Eurasian renal syndrome (HFRS) and Americas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), both characterized by endothelial manifestation. Two principal mechanisms, virus-mediated cytopathy and host-driven immunopathology, have been proposed to account for the pathological progression, while their interplay is yet to be fully explored. In this review, we synthesize the recent research on hantavirus biology, cellular entry mechanisms, and epidemiological characteristics, and particularly highlight that viral immune evasion and subsequent uncontrolled host immune responses act as the core pathogenic drivers. Hantaviruses employ diverse strategies to antagonize type I interferon signaling and autophagy, which delay early innate immune activation and enable extensive viral dissemination. The excessive activation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, combined with functionally impaired regulatory T cells and dysregulated humoral immunity, initiates severe inflammatory cascades, which in turn disrupt endothelial barrier integrity and cause organ vasculopathy. We also outline current therapeutic and preventive strategies, along with key directions for future research. A better understanding of hantavirus immunopathogenesis will help develop improved countermeasures against this zoonotic disease.

papers.full_text: nature health News ‘Desperate rodents’ pose hantavirus risk to humans — boosted by climate change and deforestation Rapid urbanization and changes in rodent behaviour increase the risk of human disease outbreaks, especially in Africa, but experts fear surveillance gaps leave most zoonotic infections undetected. By Tsitsi Bhobo W hen the Andes hantavirus cir­ culated on the M/V Hondius cruise ship, South Africa’s specialist hospitals quickly admitted infected patients and sequenced the virus. But infectious dis­ ease scientists warn that locally derived hanta­ virus strains — including the lethal Sangassou virus — are circulating undetected, hosted by native shrews, rodents and bats1. “At the moment, we believe that hanta­ virus probably is more prevalent [and] widespread than diagnosed in Africa,” says Tulio de Oliveira, Professor at Stellenbosch University, South Africa, and director of the Centre for Epidemic Response and Innova­ tion. Such infections are mainly “self-limited transmission clusters between rodents, other animals and humans,” he tells Nature Health. De Oliveira’s lab is one of a small number across Africa that test for viruses in wild animals, including rodents, bats and non- human primates. Surveillance gap Hantaviruses pose a bigger systematic dan­ ger to Africa’s public health architecture than previously thought, argued de Oliveira and colleagues in a recent article. Limited diag­ nostic and testing capacity and lack of moni­ toring infrastructure, combined with climate change and urbanization, are leading to more zoonotic outbreaks. Africa has a clinical surveillance gap, with viral spillovers probably occurring without being detected by stretched public health authorities. During the current Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, many of the early infections were suspected to be cases of malaria, leading to delays in the public health response. The DRC has the second highest bur­ den of malaria in the world, leading to tens of thousands of deaths each year. Many other zoonotic infections could be missed. Hillary Young, an ecologist at the University of California Santa Barbara, USA, notes that “we don’t know how big the burden of hanta­ virus is because we haven’t looked for it, really. We don’t have that surveillance.” “One of the acute problems facing Africa is that there is little clinical research into the ecology of hantaviruses, [such as] which specific animals host them,” she says. Such research, including genetics, would “empower scientists to map the interaction between hosts and viruses and calculate the possible harm to humans — in real time,” she adds. With surveillance capacity absent, doctors often report possible hantavirus infections as ‘fever of unknown origin’. “It’s hard, because hantavirus is another one of these diseases that kind of overlaps with lots of other unex­ plained febrile diseases,” says Young. This challenge persists despite South Africa having amongst the best infectious disease genomic surveillance infrastructure in the world. Laboratories across Africa are usually focused on supporting clinical studies in humans, but during outbreaks, resources are diverted to test animals for zoonotic infec­ tions. There are only a small number of such labs across the continent, such as the South Africa National Institute for Communicable Diseases, the Institut Pasteur de Dakar in Senegal and the Uganda Virus Research Unit. These labs act very quickly to develop reagents for new pathogens, test samples and develop metagenomics assays, but the bottleneck leads to inevitable delays, with zoonotic out­ breaks often underdiagnosed for weeks. Urbanization and deforestation Hantavirus spillover in Africa is likely to be linked to loss of biodiversity, rapid urbaniza­ tion and climate change. A recent outbreak of hantaviruses in South America spread beyond rural settings and into urban environments, Hantavirus particles under an electron microscope, with colour enhanced. CREDIT: ALFRED PASIEKA/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY/GETTY nature health News possibly because climate variations are lead­ ing to milder and shorter winters in Argentina. Rapid urbanization — widespread across the continent — leads to increased risk, as rats breed in cities where residents regularly interact with wildlife. “We’ll have a bigger pro­ liferation of concentrated rodents,” in Africa’s fast-urbanizing landscapes, says Young, lead­ ing to more zoonotic outbreaks. Young’s research has shown how declines in large wildlife in East Africa were associated with an increase in the prevalence of a rodent- borne bacterium, Bartonella, which can infect humans — providing a link between biodiver­ sity loss and zoonotic disease outbreaks2. Climate change and change of land use in Africa drive rodents to find new breeding zones in human landscapes, warns Young. Rapid expansion of cities across Africa, many without investment in sewerage, creates food and opportunities for rodent species that are already adapted to live alongside humans. This creates the conditions for ‘boom dynamics’, says Young, where rodent popula­ tions increase rapidly. This means periods of explosive, exponential growth for rat popula­ tions followed by often calamitous declines3. “You might get really desperate rodents,” she says, where the animals are “forced into kind of aggressive behaviour. Fighting in rodents can help spread disease among them at higher prevalence.” One Health The genomic surveillance labs in Africa, Latin America and Asia have considerable expertise but fewer resources than their counterparts in high-income countries, says Young. Despite these constraints, they are doing valuable work closest to the regions where zoonotic diseases are most likely to spring up. Africa is taking a lead in shifting the ‘One Health’ model towards building long-term skills, surveillance and diagnostics infrastructure in the global south, the type of capacity that remains resilient through crises. Several African countries, including the DRC and Uganda, have adopted ‘One Health’ frame­ works, an approach pioneered by Rwanda4. But such frameworks need to extend beyond the countryside and integrate with cities in Africa, rather than thinking of these urban spaces as separated from wild rural environ­ ments, says Young. De Oliveira stresses that, although hanta­ viruses are unlikely to cause large human outbreaks — because of the biology of the virus — funding cuts for global health pose challenges. There is now a “big lack of global health funding,” he says, with the US and many Euro­ pean countries “running out of money for global health because of other priorities such as defence”. Tsitsi Bhobo Johannesburg, South Africa References 1. Klempa, B. et al. Emerg. Infect. Dis. https://doi.org/10.3201/ eid1205.051487 (2006). 2. Young, H. S. et al. Proc. Natl Acad. Sci. USA https://doi.org/ 10.1073/pnas.1404958111 (2014). 3. Doebeli, M., Jaque, E. C. & Ispolatov, Y. Commun. Biol. https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-021-02021-4 (2021). 4. Henley, P. & Shyaka, A. Nat. Med. https://doi.org/10.1038/ s41591-024-03473-x (2025).

Fighting in rodents can help spread disease among them at higher prevalence.” One Health The genomic surveillance labs in Africa, Latin America and Asia have considerable expertise but fewer resources than their counterparts in high-income countries, says Young. Despite these constraints, they are doing valuable work closest to the regions where zoonotic diseases are most likely to spring up. Africa is taking a lead in shifting the ‘One Health’ model towards building long-term skills, surveillance and diagnostics infrastructure in the global south, the type of capacity that remains resilient through crises. Several African countries, including the DRC and Uganda, have adopted ‘One Health’ frame­ works, an approach pioneered by Rwanda4. But such frameworks need to extend beyond the countryside and integrate with cities in Africa, rather than thinking of these urban spaces as separated from wild rural environ­ ments, says Young. De Oliveira stresses that, although hanta­ viruses are unlikely to cause large human outbreaks — because of the biology of the virus — funding cuts for global health pose challenges. There is now a “big lack of global health funding,” he says, with the US and many Euro­ pean countries “running out of money for global health because of other priorities such as defence”. papers.abstract_zh: 自然健康新闻 ‘绝望的啮齿动物’对人类构成汉坦病毒风险——气候变暖和森林砍伐加剧了这一风险 快速城市化和啮齿动物行为的变化增加了人类疾病暴发的风险,尤其是在非洲,但专家担心监测的空白使大多数人兽共患病未被检测到。——茨西·博博 当安第斯病毒在M/V Hondius游轮上传播时,南非的专业医院迅速收治了感染患者并测序了病毒。但传染病专家警告说,本地来源的汉坦病毒株——包括致命的Sangassou病毒——正在啮齿动物、本土鼩鼱、其他动物和人类之间无检测地传播。南非圣ellenbosch大学的Tulio de Oliveira教授表示:“目前我们认为汉坦病毒在非洲的患病率和传播范围可能比已诊断的更高。”他告诉《自然健康》杂志,这类感染主要是“自我限制的传播,在啮齿动物、其他动物和人类之间形成集群。”De Oliveira的实验室是非洲少数几个对野生动物(包括啮齿动物、蝙蝠和非人类灵长类动物)进行病毒检测的实验室之一。监测的空白使汉坦病毒对非洲公共卫生体系构成更大的系统性威胁,De Oliveira及其同事在最近的一篇文章中提出了这一观点。有限的诊断和检测能力,以及缺乏监测基础设施,结合气候变化和城市化,导致了更多的人兽共患病暴发。非洲存在临床监测的空白,病毒跨物种溢出可能在未被拉伸的公共卫生机构检测到的情况下发生。在当前的刚果民主共和国邦迪布古埃博拉暴发期间,这一情况更加明显。

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus infections represent an expanding global zoonotic threat characterized by high mortality rates and limited therapeutic options. This review addresses the need for updated knowledge on hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and emerging therapeutic approaches.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study is a minireview article published in the World Journal of Virology, focusing on hantavirus infections. It was written by an invited manuscript team and discusses the global health concern posed by hantaviruses, including their association with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.
analysis.methods: The study combines classical clinical perspectives with contemporary translational research to analyze hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical features, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic approaches. It emphasizes recent advances in molecular virology, RNA-based antiviral technologies, monoclonal antibody therapy, and next-generation vaccine platforms.
analysis.main_results: The article provides an updated and integrated overview of hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic strategies, and emerging therapeutic approaches. It highlights the importance of molecular virology, RNA-based antiviral technologies, monoclonal antibody therapy, and next-generation vaccine platforms in addressing current gaps in knowledge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a call for improved surveillance, therapeutic development, and global preparedness against hantavirus infections. The novelty lies in integrating classical clinical perspectives with contemporary translational research to identify key gaps in knowledge.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform future directions for surveillance, therapeutic development, and global preparedness against hantavirus infections. They also highlight the potential of RNA-based antiviral technologies and next-generation vaccines in combating these diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review article and does not include original data or experimental results. The evidence is based on existing literature and is considered moderate in strength due to its descriptive and interpretive nature.

analysis.summary_en: This review article addresses the growing global health concern posed by hantavirus infections, emphasizing their high mortality rates and limited therapeutic options. It provides an updated overview of hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical features, and emerging therapeutic strategies, including molecular virology, RNA-based antiviral technologies, monoclonal antibody therapy, and next-generation vaccines. The study highlights key gaps in knowledge and proposes future directions for surveillance and global preparedness. While the evidence is moderate in strength due to its descriptive and interpretive nature, the findings offer valuable insights for improving diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. The study is a minireview article published in the World Journal of Virology, focusing on hantaviruses and their associated syndromes, with no specific experimental results reported.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 汉坦病毒感染代表一种日益扩大的全球人兽共患病威胁,其特征是高死亡率率和有限的治疗选择。本综述旨在更新关于汉坦病毒生物学、流行病学、临床表现和新兴治疗策略的知识。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一篇发表于《世界病毒学杂志》的短评文章,重点探讨汉坦病毒感染。该文章由受邀撰写团队完成,讨论了汉坦病毒对全球健康构成的威胁,包括其与肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒肺综合征的关联。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究结合经典临床视角与当代转化研究,分析汉坦病毒的生物学、流行病学、临床特征、诊断策略和治疗方案。它强调了分子病毒学、基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术、单克隆抗体疗法以及下一代疫苗平台的最新进展。
elements_zh.main_results: 本文提供了关于汉坦病毒生物学、流行病学、临床表现、诊断策略和新兴治疗方案的更新且综合的概述。它突出了分子病毒学、基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术、单克隆抗体疗法以及下一代疫苗平台在解决当前知识空白中的重要性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为对改进监测、治疗开发和全球应对汉坦病毒感染的呼吁。其新颖之处在于将经典临床视角与当代转化研究相结合,以识别知识中的关键空白。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为监测、治疗开发和全球应对汉坦病毒感染提供未来方向。它们还突出了基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术和下一代疫苗在对抗这些疾病方面的潜力。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus infections represent an expanding global zoonotic threat characterized by high mortality rates and limited therapeutic options. This review addresses the need for updated knowledge on hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and emerging therapeutic approaches.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study is a minireview article published in the World Journal of Virology, focusing on hantavirus infections. It was written by an invited manuscript team and discusses the global health concern posed by hantaviruses, including their association with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.
analysis_en.methods: The study combines classical clinical perspectives with contemporary translational research to analyze hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical features, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic approaches. It emphasizes recent advances in molecular virology, RNA-based antiviral technologies, monoclonal antibody therapy, and next-generation vaccine platforms.
analysis_en.main_results: The article provides an updated and integrated overview of hantavirus biology, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic strategies, and emerging therapeutic approaches. It highlights the importance of molecular virology, RNA-based antiviral technologies, monoclonal antibody therapy, and next-generation vaccine platforms in addressing current gaps in knowledge.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a call for improved surveillance, therapeutic development, and global preparedness against hantavirus infections. The novelty lies in integrating classical clinical perspectives with contemporary translational research to identify key gaps in knowledge.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform future directions for surveillance, therapeutic development, and global preparedness against hantavirus infections. They also highlight the potential of RNA-based antiviral technologies and next-generation vaccines in combating these diseases.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review article and does not include original data or experimental results. The evidence is based on existing literature and is considered moderate in strength due to its descriptive and interpretive nature.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 汉坦病毒感染代表一种日益扩大的全球人兽共患病威胁,其特征是高死亡率率和有限的治疗选择。本综述旨在更新关于汉坦病毒生物学、流行病学、临床表现和新兴治疗策略的知识。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一篇发表于《世界病毒学杂志》的短评文章,重点探讨汉坦病毒感染。该文章由受邀撰写团队完成,讨论了汉坦病毒对全球健康构成的威胁,包括其与肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒肺综合征的关联。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究结合经典临床视角与当代转化研究,分析汉坦病毒的生物学、流行病学、临床特征、诊断策略和治疗方案。它强调了分子病毒学、基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术、单克隆抗体疗法以及下一代疫苗平台的最新进展。
analysis_zh.main_results: 本文提供了关于汉坦病毒生物学、流行病学、临床表现、诊断策略和新兴治疗方案的更新且综合的概述。它突出了分子病毒学、基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术、单克隆抗体疗法以及下一代疫苗平台在解决当前知识空白中的重要性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为对改进监测、治疗开发和全球应对汉坦病毒感染的呼吁。其新颖之处在于将经典临床视角与当代转化研究相结合,以识别知识中的关键空白。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为监测、治疗开发和全球应对汉坦病毒感染提供未来方向。它们还突出了基于RNA的抗病毒药物技术和下一代疫苗在对抗这些疾病方面的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一篇综述文章,不包含原始数据或实验结果。其证据基于现有文献,由于其描述性和解释性性质,证据强度被认为是中等的。

papers.title: A systematic review of ultrasound to predict severe disease in patients with dengue and other viral infections associated with hemorrhagic fevers.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral infections associated with hemorrhagic fevers (VaHFs) cause millions of cases each year across a broad geography with severity ranging from asymptomatic cases to clinical disease with a high case fatality rate. Commonalities in pathophysiology across VaHFs include vascular damage and plasma leakage with the possibility of hemorrhage, organ failure, shock, and death. These changes are seen on autopsy, and evidence of plasma leakage can be readily detected on ultrasound. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review to assess ultrasound findings in VaHFs and their ability to predict severe disease (PROSPERO CRD42024620862). PubMed was searched through May 2025. Any articles presenting original, patient-level findings on ultrasound in VaHFs with serologic and/or molecular confirmation were included. Case series and duplicative datasets were excluded. A QUADAS-2 tool was used to assess bias. Study level characteristics and patient-level data on the ultrasound findings were extracted. The crude proportions of ultrasound findings were reported, and weighted meta-analysis using a random-effects model was performed and displayed in forest plots when the data allowed. Sensitivity, specificity, and positive/negative likelihood ratios for severe disease were calculated and visualized using a random effects model in SROC plots when the data allowed. RESULTS: In total, 457 unique publications were screened for inclusion, and 56 publications comprising 6979 participants were included in the review, including 44 publications (6189 participants) on dengue, six (494 participants) on Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, three (134 participants) on hantavirus disease, two (116 participants) on yellow fever, and one (46 participants) on Lassa fever. Participants were most often recruited while acutely sick during periods of high transmission at tertiary care centers. Ultrasound findings included gallbladder wall thickening, ascites, pleural effusions and abnormal lung ultrasound, pericardial effusions, abdominal lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, abnormal pancreatic ultrasound, and hyperechoic kidneys or liver. Pericardial effusions and several other findings were associated with severe disease. CONCLUSIONS: Common pathophysiology leading to plasma leakage results in sonographic signs across viral infections associated with hemorrhagic fevers, and some findings can help predict severe disease. Important limitations included reliance on a single database and possibility of missing manuscripts from local journals, the small number of publications on non-dengue VaHFs, patient recruitment overwhelmingly from the in-hospital setting at tertiary referral centers during high-transmission periods, high degree of heterogeneity, and bias in the timing domain among the studies on dengue. We first propose ultrasound findings be incorporated into new definitions of severity for VaHFs and then introduce an Ultrasound-based assessment of Plasma leakage Severity (UPS) as a hypothesis generating framework to help guide future, prospective research. We discuss some virus and organ-specific considerations and conclude with detailed considerations for future research.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:与出血热(VaHF)相关的病毒感染每年在广泛的地区引起数百万例病例,其严重程度从无症状病例到病死率较高的临床疾病。VaHF 病理生理学的共同点包括血管损伤和血浆渗漏,可能导致出血、器官衰竭、休克和死亡。这些变化可以在尸检中看到,并且可以通过超声波轻松检测到血浆渗漏的证据。方法:我们进行了系统评价,以评估 VaHF 的超声检查结果及其预测严重疾病的能力 (PROSPERO CRD42024620862)。PubMed 的检索截止日期为 2025 年 5 月。任何介绍 VaHF 超声检查的原始患者水平结果并经血清学和/或分子证实的文章均被纳入。病例系列和重复数据集被排除在外。使用 QUADAS-2 工具来评估偏差。提取了超声结果的研究水平特征和患者水平数据。报告了超声检查结果的粗略比例,并使用随机效应模型进行了加权荟萃分析,并在数据允许时将其显示在森林图中。当数据允许时,使用 SROC 图中的随机效应模型计算并可视化严重疾病的敏感性、特异性和阳性/阴性似然比。结果:总共筛选了 457 篇独特的出版物,其中 56 篇出版物(6979 名参与者)被纳入审查,其中 44 篇关于登革热的出版物(6189 名参与者),6 篇关于克里米亚-刚果出血热的出版物(494 名参与者),3 篇关于汉坦病毒病的出版物(134 名参与者),2 篇关于黄热病的出版物(116 名参与者),以及 1 篇关于拉沙热的出版物(46 名参与者)发烧。参与者最常在三级护理中心的 传播 高水平期间重病时被招募。超声检查结果包括胆囊壁增厚、腹水、胸腔积液和肺部超声异常、心包积液、腹部淋巴结肿大、脾肿大、胰腺超声异常以及肾脏或肝脏高回声。心包积液和其他一些发现与严重疾病有关。结论:导致血浆渗漏的常见病理生理学导致与出血热相关的病毒感染的超声征象,并且一些发现可以帮助预测严重疾病。重要的局限性包括对单一数据库的依赖以及当地期刊手稿丢失的可能性、非登革热 VaHF 的出版物数量较少、在高 传播 时期绝大多数患者从三级转诊中心的院内环境中招募、高度异质性以及登革热研究中时间域的偏差。我们首先建议将超声发现纳入 VaHF 严重程度的新定义中,然后引入基于超声的血浆泄漏严重程度 (UPS) 评估,作为假设生成框架,以帮助指导未来的前瞻性研究。我们讨论了一些病毒和器官特异性的考虑因素,并总结了未来研究的详细考虑因素。

papers.title: Multi-omics Reveals Divergent Endothelial Molecular Responses to New and Old World Hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause vascular leakage syndromes that vary in clinical manifestation and severity. Although tissue tropism contributes to these differences, both Old and New World hantaviruses infect endothelial cells, where species-specific disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Here we integrated time-resolved global RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry proteomics, and phosphoproteomics of human endothelial cells infected with New World Andes virus (ANDV) or Old World Hantaan virus (HTNV). Despite equivalent early viral RNA and protein levels, ANDV elicited a stronger innate immune protein response, preceding its restriction while HTNV replication continued. At later stages of infection, HTNV induced downregulation of cytoskeletal and junctional protein phosphorylation, accompanied by visual disruption of cellular actin architecture. Additionally, ANDV induced heightened activity of ERBB-family kinases, whose chemical inhibition by neratinib and afatinib reduced viral replication. Together, these data define species-specific responses in endothelial cells, identify druggable host targets, and reveal mechanisms with relevance to divergent vascular leakage symptomology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the divergent molecular responses of endothelial cells to New World Andes virus (ANDV) and Old World Hantaan virus (HTNV), addressing the knowledge gap in species-specific disease phenotypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the integration of time-resolved global RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry proteomics, and phosphoproteomics of human endothelial cells infected with ANDV or HTNV.
analysis.methods: Time-resolved global RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry proteomics, and phosphoproteomics were used to analyze human endothelial cells infected with ANDV or HTNV.
analysis.main_results: ANDV elicited a stronger innate immune protein response early in infection, while HTNV induced downregulation of cytoskeletal and junctional protein phosphorylation, leading to visual disruption of cellular actin architecture.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified species-specific responses in endothelial cells, highlighting the importance of ERBB-family kinases as druggable host targets, and revealed mechanisms relevant to divergent vascular leakage symptomology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for hantavirus infections, particularly in understanding the mechanisms underlying different clinical manifestations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of human endothelial cells and does not address the full complexity of hantavirus infection in vivo, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the molecular responses of human endothelial cells to New World Andes virus (ANDV) and Old World Hantaan virus (HTNV), identifying species-specific mechanisms and potential druggable targets.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及感染 ANDV 或 HTNV 的人内皮细胞的时间分辨全局 RNA 测序、质谱蛋白质组学和磷酸蛋白质组学的整合。
elements_zh.methods: 使用时间分辨全局 RNA 测序、质谱蛋白质组学和磷酸蛋白质组学来分析感染 ANDV 或 HTNV 的人内皮细胞。
elements_zh.main_results: ANDV 在感染早期引发更强的先天免疫蛋白反应,而 HTNV 诱导细胞骨架和连接蛋白磷酸化下调,导致细胞肌动蛋白结构的视觉破坏。

papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses cause vascular leakage syndromes that vary in clinical manifestation and severity. Although tissue tropism contributes to these differences, both Old and New World hantaviruses infect endothelial cells, where species-specific disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Here we integrated time-resolved global RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry proteomics, and phosphoproteomics of human endothelial cells infected with New World Andes virus (ANDV) or Old World Hantaan virus (HTNV). Despite equivalent early viral RNA and protein levels, ANDV elicited a stronger innate immune protein response, preceding its restriction while HTNV replication continued. At later stages of infection, HTNV induced downregulation of cytoskeletal and junctional protein phosphorylation, accompanied by visual disruption of cellular actin architecture. Additionally, ANDV induced heightened activity of ERBB-family kinases, whose chemical inhibition by neratinib and afatinib reduced viral replication. Together, these data define species-specific responses in endothelial cells, identify druggable host targets, and reveal mechanisms with relevance to divergent vascular leakage symptomology.

papers.title: A multispecies convergence zone: viral diversity and zoonotic spillover potential at Cambodia’s cross-border rodent trade hub
papers.abstract: Live animal trade interfaces may increase opportunities for zoonotic pathogen exposure through multispecies aggregation and repeated human-animal contact, yet systematic multi-host surveillance remains limited. We investigated a cross-border rodent trade hub in Chrey Thom, Cambodia, where rodents from multiple provinces were consolidated for export to Vietnam. This multispecies convergence zone provided an opportunity to characterize viral diversity, detection frequency, and behavioural factors associated with spillover potential. From 2015 to 2018, we conducted repeated cross-sectional surveillance over four years among rodents, domestic animals, and humans using consensus polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays targeting nine viral families. Zoonotic-exposure questionnaires were administered to community members and febrile hospital patients. We estimated detection frequencies by host group and described reported behaviours and exposure awareness. Among 2,618 specimens from 1,005 animals and 342 humans, 15.3% of specimens and 21.5% of individuals were positive, all among animals, with 12 distinct viruses identified. Rodents and poultry had the highest detection rates, at 34.7% and 33.9%, respectively. Coronaviruses predominated in rodents (34.4%), including an HKU1-like betacoronavirus. Rattus losea had 76.2% positivity, and Seoul virus was detected in the atypical host Rattus argentiventer . In poultry, PREDICT-CoV-100, infectious bronchitis virus, and Newcastle disease virus were detected; infectious bronchitis virus was molecularly documented in Cambodia for the first time. Influenza A(H5) was detected in ducks and A(H9) in chickens. No viruses were detected by PCR in humans. High-risk animal-contact behaviours were common in both participant groups, and only 10.7% recognized zoonotic transmission routes. Diverse viruses of zoonotic or veterinary relevance were detected in animals at this cross-border rodent trade hub. Frequent viral RNA detection in traded rodents and poultry, combined with common human-animal contact and limited awareness of zoonotic transmission routes, supports integrated One Health surveillance at wildlife trade interfaces. These data provide a rare pre-COVID baseline for assessing how evolving trade pathways may influence future interface-level spillover risk.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a cross-border rodent trade hub in Cambodia to assess zoonotic spillover potential. It found that rodents and poultry carried a high diversity of viruses, including Seoul virus, which is associated with hantavirus research. The study emphasized the role of live animal trade in increasing pathogen exposure through multispecies aggregation and human-animal contact. It also noted that only 10.7% of participants recognized zoonotic transmission routes, underscoring the need for improved awareness. The findings support integrated One Health surveillance at wildlife trade interfaces and provide a pre-COVID baseline for future risk assessments. However, the study's focus on animal specimens and lack of human viral detection limit its scope, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估柬埔寨跨境啮齿动物贸易中心人畜共患 跨物种溢出 的潜力,强调在活体动物贸易界面中系统性多 宿主 监测 的需求,因为它们在通过多物种聚集和人与动物接触增加病原体暴露方面发挥着作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2015 年至 2018 年在柬埔寨 Chrey Thom 的一个跨境啮齿动物贸易中心进行,涉及 1,005 只动物和 342 人。从啮齿动物、家畜和人类身上采集样本,以评估病毒多样性和 跨物种溢出 潜力。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用针对九个病毒家族的共识聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测进行了重复的横截面 监测。对社区成员和发热医院患者进行人畜共患病暴露调查问卷,以收集行为和意识数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 2,618 份样本中,15.3% 呈阳性,全部来自动物,并鉴定出 12 种不同的病毒。啮齿动物和家禽的检出率最高,分别为34.7%和33.9%。冠状病毒,包括类似 HKU1 的 β 冠状病毒,在啮齿类动物中占主导地位。在银毛家鼠中检测到首尔病毒,在家禽中检测到 PREDICT-CoV-100、传染性支气管炎病毒和新城疫病毒。在鸭中检测到甲型(H5)流感,在鸡中检测到甲型(H9)流感。通过 PCR 在人体中未检测到病毒。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,交易的啮齿动物和家禽携带多种病毒,包括与汉坦病毒研究相关的首尔病毒。该研究强调了了解人与动物接触行为以及了解此类环境中人畜共患病 传播 路线的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果支持在野生动物贸易界面需要集成 One Health 监测 来监测人畜共患病原体并评估 跨物种溢出 风险。它们还提供了一个罕见的新冠疫情前基线,用于评估不断变化的贸易路径如何影响未来的 跨物种溢出 潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注动物标本且缺乏人类病毒检测而受到限制。尽管存在这些局限性,但由于全面的 监测 方法以及对多种具有潜在人畜共患病相关性的病毒的识别,证据的强度适中。

papers.source_body_en: Live animal trade interfaces may increase opportunities for zoonotic pathogen exposure through multispecies aggregation and repeated human-animal contact, yet systematic multi-host surveillance remains limited. We investigated a cross-border rodent trade hub in Chrey Thom, Cambodia, where rodents from multiple provinces were consolidated for export to Vietnam. This multispecies convergence zone provided an opportunity to characterize viral diversity, detection frequency, and behavioural factors associated with spillover potential. From 2015 to 2018, we conducted repeated cross-sectional surveillance over four years among rodents, domestic animals, and humans using consensus polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays targeting nine viral families. Zoonotic-exposure questionnaires were administered to community members and febrile hospital patients. We estimated detection frequencies by host group and described reported behaviours and exposure awareness. Among 2,618 specimens from 1,005 animals and 342 humans, 15.3% of specimens and 21.5% of individuals were positive, all among animals, with 12 distinct viruses identified. Rodents and poultry had the highest detection rates, at 34.7% and 33.9%, respectively. Coronaviruses predominated in rodents (34.4%), including an HKU1-like betacoronavirus. Rattus losea had 76.2% positivity, and Seoul virus was detected in the atypical host Rattus argentiventer . In poultry, PREDICT-CoV-100, infectious bronchitis virus, and Newcastle disease virus were detected; infectious bronchitis virus was molecularly documented in Cambodia for the first time. Influenza A(H5) was detected in ducks and A(H9) in chickens. No viruses were detected by PCR in humans. High-risk animal-contact behaviours were common in both participant groups, and only 10.7% recognized zoonotic transmission routes. Diverse viruses of zoonotic or veterinary relevance were detected in animals at this cross-border rodent trade hub. Frequent viral RNA detection in traded rodents and poultry, combined with common human-animal contact and limited awareness of zoonotic transmission routes, supports integrated One Health surveillance at wildlife trade interfaces. These data provide a rare pre-COVID baseline for assessing how evolving trade pathways may influence future interface-level spillover risk.
papers.abstract_zh: 活体动物贸易界面可能会通过多物种聚集和重复的人与动物接触增加人畜共患病原体暴露的机会,但系统性的多 宿主 监测 仍然有限。我们调查了柬埔寨 Chrey Thom 的一个跨境啮齿动物贸易中心,来自多个省份的啮齿动物被集中在一起出口到越南。这个多物种融合区提供了一个机会来表征病毒多样性、检测频率以及与 跨物种溢出 潜力相关的行为因素。从 2015 年到 2018 年,我们使用针对 9 个病毒家族的共识聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测,在四年多的时间里,在啮齿动物、家畜和人类中进行了重复的横断面 监测。对社区成员和发热医院患者进行了人畜共患病暴露调查问卷。我们估计了 宿主 组的检测频率,并描述了报告的行为和暴露意识。在来自 1,005 只动物和 342 名人类的 2,618 份样本中,15.3% 的样本和 21.5% 的个体呈阳性,全部为动物,并鉴定出 12 种不同的病毒。啮齿动物和家禽的检出率最高,分别为34.7%和33.9%。冠状病毒在啮齿动物中占主导地位(34.4%),包括类似 HKU1 的 β 冠状病毒。黄鼠阳性率为76.2%,非典型宿主黄鼠中检出首尔病毒。在家禽中检测到 PREDICT-CoV-100、传染性支气管炎病毒和新城疫病毒;柬埔寨首次对传染性支气管炎病毒进行分子记录。在鸭中检测到甲型(H5)流感,在鸡中检测到甲型(H9)流感。通过 PCR 在人体中未检测到病毒。高风险动物接触行为在两个参与者组中都很常见,只有 10.7% 的人认识到人畜共患 传播 途径。在这个跨境啮齿动物贸易中心的动物体内检测到了多种与人畜共患或兽医相关的病毒。对交易的啮齿动物和家禽进行频繁的病毒 RNA 检测,加上常见的人与动物接触以及对人畜共患 传播 途径的有限认识,支持在野生动物贸易界面整合 One Health 传播。这些数据为评估不断变化的贸易路径如何影响未来界面级 跨物种溢出 风险提供了罕见的新冠疫情前基线。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估柬埔寨跨境啮齿动物贸易中心人畜共患 跨物种溢出 的潜力,强调在活体动物贸易界面中系统性多 宿主 监测 的需求,因为它们在通过多物种聚集和人与动物接触增加病原体暴露方面发挥着作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2015 年至 2018 年在柬埔寨 Chrey Thom 的一个跨境啮齿动物贸易中心进行,涉及 1,005 只动物和 342 人。从啮齿动物、家畜和人类身上采集样本,以评估病毒多样性和 跨物种溢出 潜力。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用针对九个病毒家族的共识聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测进行了重复的横截面 监测。对社区成员和发热医院患者进行人畜共患病暴露调查问卷,以收集行为和意识数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 2,618 份样本中,15.3% 呈阳性,全部来自动物,并鉴定出 12 种不同的病毒。啮齿动物和家禽的检出率最高,分别为34.7%和33.9%。冠状病毒,包括类似 HKU1 的 β 冠状病毒,在啮齿类动物中占主导地位。在银毛家鼠中检测到首尔病毒,在家禽中检测到 PREDICT-CoV-100、传染性支气管炎病毒和新城疫病毒。在鸭中检测到甲型(H5)流感,在鸡中检测到甲型(H9)流感。通过 PCR 在人体中未检测到病毒。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,交易的啮齿动物和家禽携带多种病毒,包括与汉坦病毒研究相关的首尔病毒。该研究强调了了解人与动物接触行为以及了解此类环境中人畜共患病 传播 路线的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果支持在野生动物贸易界面需要集成 One Health 监测 来监测人畜共患病原体并评估 跨物种溢出 风险。它们还提供了一个罕见的新冠疫情前基线,用于评估不断变化的贸易路径如何影响未来的 跨物种溢出 潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注动物标本且缺乏人类病毒检测而受到限制。尽管存在这些局限性,但由于全面的 监测 方法以及对多种具有潜在人畜共患病相关性的病毒的识别,证据的强度适中。

news.content: Feedback | Friday, September 18, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Evacuations planned as suspected hantavirus outbreak traps 150 on ship off Cape Verde 05/05/26 | 12:23 pm | Cape Verde | The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health | West Africa Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Evacuations planned as suspected hantavirus outbreak traps 150 on ship off Cape Verde A sign warns of hantavirus contamination in an old guard shack at the EBR-1 Atomic Museum. (Photo by: Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) Medics were working on Monday to evacuate two people with symptoms of the deadly hantavirus after a suspected outbreak on a luxury cruise ship held off West Africa carrying mostly British, American and Spanish passengers, officials said. Around 150 people were still stuck on the vessel after three people – a Dutch couple and a German national – died, and others fell ill, including a Briton who left the vessel and was being treated in South Africa, authorities added. The Netherlands’ National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM), which is assisting with the outbreak, said hantavirus had been confirmed in one of the patients showing symptoms. A source briefed on the matter said that the Dutch woman who died had tested positive for the virus as well. RIVM said it was still unclear if the other people with symptoms also had the virus, or if the other deaths were also caused by the virus. Hantavirus, which can cause fatal respiratory illness, can be spread when particles from rodent droppings or urine become airborne. It does not transfer easily between humans. There are no specific drugs to treat the disease, so treatment focuses on supportive care, including putting patients on ventilators in severe cases. The World Health Organization said the risk to the wider public was low and there was no need for panic or travel restrictions. But authorities in the island nation of Cape Verde said they had not allowed Dutch-flagged MV Hondius to dock as a precaution. The WHO said in a statement that it had identified seven cases of hantavirus aboard the luxury cruise ship, including two laboratory confirmed cases and five suspected cases. ‘A LOT OF UNCERTAINTY’ “We’re not just headlines: we’re people with families, with lives, with people waiting for us at home,” Jake Rosmarin, a U.S. travel blogger, said in a tearful Instagram video post from the ship on Monday. “There is a lot of uncertainty and that is the hardest part,” he added. A spokesperson for the ship’s Netherlands-based operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, said that, as a precaution, all passengers were instructed to remain inside their cabins to prevent any potential spread of the virus. Although human-to-human transmission is rare, the incubation period can last several weeks, meaning some people may not yet be showing symptoms. Oceanwide Expeditions was trying to arrange the repatriation of two crew members with symptoms of the disease – one British and one Dutch – along with the body of the German national and a “guest closely associated with the deceased” who does not have symptoms. The company said it was looking into whether passengers could be screened and disembarked on the islands of Las Palmas and Tenerife. Spanish authorities said they had not yet received a request for the ship to dock and disembark passengers there. The Dutch Foreign Affairs Ministry, which Oceanwide Expeditions said would be the one making the request, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Hondius left Ushuaia in southern Argentina in March, according to company documentation, on a voyage marketed as an Antarctic nature expedition, with berth prices ranging from 14,000 to 22,000 euros ($16,000-$25,000). It travelled past mainland Antarctica, the Falklands, South Georgia, Nightingale Island, Tristan, St Helena, and Ascension before reaching Cape Verdean waters on May 3. South Africa’s Health Department confirmed two of the dead were Dutch nationals: a 70-year-old man, who died on St Helena on April 11, and his wife, 69, who died in South Africa after collapsing at O.R. Tambo International Airport. The British man being treated in a private clinic in Johannesburg became ill on April 27, while the German victim on the ship died on May 2, Oceanwide Expeditions said. SOURCE NOT YET CLEAR Hantavirus usually begins with flu-like symptoms, such as fatigue and fever, one to eight weeks after exposure. A spokesperson for the RIVM said the source of the outbreak was unclear. “You could imagine, for example, that rats on board the ship transmitted the virus,” he said. “But another possibility is that during a stop somewhere in South America, people were infected, for instance via mice, and became ill that way.” Daniel Bausch, a visiting professor at the Geneva Graduate Institute in Switzerland, said there was some evidence of human-to-human transmission in the Andes Virus, a species of hantavirus found in Argentina and Chile. “So it’s significant that this cruise ship started its journey in Argentina,” he said. “The good news is ... this is not going to be a big outbreak,” he added. analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred on a luxury cruise ship off Cape Verde, which was carrying mostly British, American, and Spanish passengers. The ship, MV Hondius, departed from Ushuaia, Argentina, in March 2026, and traveled through South America and the South Atlantic before reaching Cape Verdean waters on May 3.
analysis.event: A suspected hantavirus outbreak was reported on a cruise ship off Cape Verde, with three deaths and several illnesses among passengers. The Netherlands’ National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) confirmed the presence of hantavirus in one patient and stated that the source of the outbreak was unclear.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Seven cases of hantavirus were identified on the ship, including two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases. The Dutch Foreign Affairs Ministry and Cape Verde authorities were involved in managing the situation, with the ship not allowed to dock as a precaution. The World Health Organization noted the risk to the wider public was low, and there was no need for panic or travel restrictions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Authorities are investigating the source of the outbreak, which may involve rodents on board or exposure during stops in South America. The Dutch woman who died tested positive for the virus, but it remains unclear if the other symptomatic individuals also had the virus. The ship’s operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, is arranging repatriation and considering screening passengers for disembarkation.

analysis.brief_en: A suspected hantavirus outbreak has been reported on a luxury cruise ship, MV Hondius, off Cape Verde, which is carrying British, American, and Spanish passengers. The Netherlands’ National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) confirmed the presence of hantavirus in one patient, while the deaths of three individuals—two Dutch nationals and a German national—were linked to the outbreak. The British man, who became ill on April 27, is being treated in South Africa. The World Health Organization stated the risk to the wider public is low, and there is no need for panic or travel restrictions. However, Cape Verde authorities have not allowed the ship to dock as a precaution. Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship’s operator, is working to arrange repatriation and screen passengers for disembarkation. The source of the outbreak remains unclear, with possibilities including rodent transmission on board or exposure during stops in South America. The outbreak has raised concerns about the potential spread of the virus, which can cause severe respiratory illness and is typically spread through rodent droppings or urine. There are no specific drugs to treat hantavirus, and treatment focuses on supportive care, such as ventilator support in severe cases. The situation is under investigation, with no definitive conclusions yet.

news.content_zh: 据报道,佛得角附近一艘豪华游轮 MV Hondius 上有一艘疑似汉坦病毒暴发,该游轮载有英国、美国和西班牙乘客。荷兰国家公共卫生与环境研究所 (RIVM) 证实一名患者体内存在 汉坦病毒,而三人(两名荷兰国民和一名德国国民)的死亡与 暴发 有关。这名英国男子于4月27日发病,目前正在南非接受治疗。世界卫生组织表示,广大公众面临的风险较低,无需恐慌或旅行限制。然而,作为预防措施,佛得角当局不允许该船靠岸。该船的运营商 Oceanwide Expeditions 正在努力安排遣返并筛查乘客下船。暴发 的来源尚不清楚,可能包括船上的啮齿动物 传播 或在南美停留期间接触到的病毒。暴发 引起了人们对该病毒潜在传播的担忧,该病毒可能导致严重的呼吸道疾病,通常通过啮齿动物的粪便或尿液传播。目前尚无治疗汉坦病毒的特效药物,治疗侧重于支持治疗,例如重症病例的呼吸机支持。目前情况正在调查中,目前还没有明确的结论。

news.content: Feedback | Friday, September 18, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Passengers begin evacuating from cruise ship hit by hantavirus 10/05/26 | 5:16 pm Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Passengers begin evacuating from cruise ship hit by hantavirus Groups of passengers and crew disembarked from a cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak on Sunday to be evacuated to their respective countries in a process overseen by global health officials and expected to last until Monday. The passengers, none of whom were showing symptoms of the virus, were taken to Tenerife airport in military buses to be evacuated from the island in government planes sent by their respective countries, government officials said, emphasising that they will have no contact with the public. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended a 42-day quarantine for all passengers from the boat from Sunday. Planes for the Spanish and French nationals had departed by 1130 GMT. Canada, the Netherlands, the UK, Turkey, Ireland, and the United States were listed by Spanish health minister Monica Garcia as the next countries to evacuate their citizens, with the Dutch plane also due to take Germans, Belgians and Greeks. A plane from Australia which would transport its citizens as well as passengers from New Zealand and other unspecified Asian countries was due to land on Monday and depart by the afternoon, Garcia said. Hantavirus, which is usually spread by rodents but can in rare cases be transmitted person-to-person, was first detected on May 2, 21 days after the first passenger died, by South African health officials testing a British man who was in intensive care. Two other former passengers have died since. The luxury cruise ship left for Spain on Wednesday from the coast of Cape Verde after the WHO and European Union asked the country to manage the evacuation of passengers after the hantavirus outbreak was detected. The agency said the first case may have been infected before boarding, possibly during travel in Argentina and Chile, with later spread likely occurring on the ship. NO RODENTS DETECTED ON THE SHIP The WHO said in an update on Friday that eight people no longer on the ship had fallen ill, including the three who died – a Dutch couple and a German national. Of the eight, six are confirmed to have contracted the virus. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, in Tenerife to oversee the evacuation, said on Sunday that WHO experts were working alongside Spanish health officials to test the passengers. One Spanish woman, who was suspected of having the virus after sharing a flight with one of the patients who later died, tested negative late on Saturday. The UK military has parachuted a specialist team onto the remote island of Tristan da Cunha to provide medical support to the second suspected case, a British man who was a passenger on the ship and lives on the island in the South Atlantic. Four patients remain hospitalized in South Africa, the Netherlands and Switzerland, while a suspected case sent to Germany tested negative. All passengers on the MV Hondius are considered high-risk contacts as a precautionary measure, Europe’s public health agency said late on Saturday as part of its rapid scientific advice, adding that the risk to the general population remains low. Spain’s health ministry said in a report on the ship passing the appropriate health checks: “There are more than 500 cruise ships a year that come from Argentina and Chile, which is home to the virus, and yet an outbreak of this illness has never happened in European territory so the possibility it happens in relation to this ship is remote.” It also said rodents had not been detected aboard the ship. Passengers will not leave the boat until their allocated evacuation plane has arrived, Spanish officials said. Thirty crew members will remain on board and sail to the Netherlands where the ship will be disinfected. news.content_original: Feedback | Friday, September 18, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Passengers begin evacuating from cruise ship hit by hantavirus 10/05/26 | 5:16 pm Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Passengers begin evacuating from cruise ship hit by hantavirus Groups of passengers and crew disembarked from a cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak on Sunday to be evacuated to their respective countries in a process overseen by global health officials and expected to last until Monday. The passengers, none of whom were showing symptoms of the virus, were taken to Tenerife airport in military buses to be evacuated from the island in government planes sent by their respective countries, government officials said, emphasising that they will have no contact with the public. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended a 42-day quarantine for all passengers from the boat from Sunday. Planes for the Spanish and French nationals had departed by 1130 GMT. Canada, the Netherlands, the UK, Turkey, Ireland, and the United States were listed by Spanish health minister Monica Garcia as the next countries to evacuate their citizens, with the Dutch plane also due to take Germans, Belgians and Greeks. A plane from Australia which would transport its citizens as well as passengers from New Zealand and other unspecified Asian countries was due to land on Monday and depart by the afternoon, Garcia said. Hantavirus, which is usually spread by rodents but can in rare cases be transmitted person-to-person, was first detected on May 2, 21 days after the first passenger died, by South African health officials testing a British man who was in intensive care. Two other former passengers have died since. The luxury cruise ship left for Spain on Wednesday from the coast of Cape Verde after the WHO and European Union asked the country to manage the evacuation of passengers after the hantavirus outbreak was detected. The agency said the first case may have been infected before boarding, possibly during travel in Argentina and Chile, with later spread likely occurring on the ship. NO RODENTS DETECTED ON THE SHIP The WHO said in an update on Friday that eight people no longer on the ship had fallen ill, including the three who died – a Dutch couple and a German national. Of the eight, six are confirmed to have contracted the virus. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, in Tenerife to oversee the evacuation, said on Sunday that WHO experts were working alongside Spanish health officials to test the passengers. One Spanish woman, who was suspected of having the virus after sharing a flight with one of the patients who later died, tested negative late on Saturday. The UK military has parachuted a specialist team onto the remote island of Tristan da Cunha to provide medical support to the second suspected case, a British man who was a passenger on the ship and lives on the island in the South Atlantic. Four patients remain hospitalized in South Africa, the Netherlands and Switzerland, while a suspected case sent to Germany tested negative. All passengers on the MV Hondius are considered high-risk contacts as a precautionary measure, Europe’s public health agency said late on Saturday as part of its rapid scientific advice, adding that the risk to the general population remains low. Spain’s health ministry said in a report on the ship passing the appropriate health checks: “There are more than 500 cruise ships a year that come from Argentina and Chile, which is home to the virus, and yet an outbreak of this illness has never happened in European territory so the possibility it happens in relation to this ship is remote.” It also said rodents had not been detected aboard the ship. Passengers will not leave the boat until their allocated evacuation plane has arrived, Spanish officials said. Thirty crew members will remain on board and sail to the Netherlands where the ship will be disinfected. OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Popular Reads Judge blocks adding Trump tribute to Kennedy Center in scathing ruling Sep 15 Twin sisters conjoined at head underwent successful separation surgery: Hospital 1 day ago Man arrested in death of woman found hanging from tree in Mississippi Sep 12 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC. OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Popular Reads Judge blocks adding Trump tribute to Kennedy Center in scathing ruling Sep 15 Twin sisters conjoined at head underwent successful separation surgery: Hospital 1 day ago Man arrested in death of woman found hanging from tree in Mississippi Sep 12 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC.
